tools.title: PackageCreator Dockable Panel
tools.purpose: Deliver a Revit dockable panel that reproduces as much practical functionality as possible from the standalone Issue Package Creator app while remaining native to pyRevit workflows. The panel must stay open while users continue modeling and provide live issue-package context for the active Revit project.
notes: Keep pushbutton script thin and delegate behavior to reusable library modules. Register and own dockable pane lifecycle centrally, not inside ad hoc UI handlers. Keep long-running or dependency-heavy operations out of WPF click handlers. Preserve audit-style outcomes: clear statuses, counts, warnings, and report paths. Treat CPython-only dependencies as helper-side concerns, not direct IronPython panel logic. Keep panel useful at narrow width and safe while user continues Revit work.

Start implementation with pane lifecycle and state contract, then wire actions one by one. Keep UI handlers thin and route all heavy operations through orchestrator methods. Preserve human-readable status and diagnostics from every helper action.

tools.title: View Filter Editor
tools.function: `script.py` — thin entry point: loads engine + UI, calls `main()` `ViewFilterEditor.xaml` — WPF layout (app bar, search toolbar, tabbed DataGrids, right-panel editor, footer)
tools.purpose: Browse all applied view filters in the project, split between View Templates and regular views. Allows filtering, sorting, and editing of per-view filter overrides — Enable, Visibility, Projection/Surface (Lines, Patterns, Transparency), Cut (Lines, Patterns), and Halftone — mirroring Revit's native Filters tab.
notes: Never acquire `doc` at module level in engine or UI — always passed from `script.py` Transaction must be a plain `Start()/Commit()/RollBack()` sequence (IronPython 2.7 does not support `with Transaction(...)`) `ViewFilterEditorWindow` extends `forms.WPFWindow`; XAML path is always passed explicitly from the bundle dir All writes go through `apply_filter_overrides(doc, payload)` in the engine — UI only stages changes

Colour swatches are clickable Borders; colours use `#RRGGBB` hex strings internally Pattern combos are populated at row-select time from `collect_fill_patterns(doc)` Detail panel is hidden until a DataGrid row is selected; `Stage Changes` marks row dirty Only dirty rows are committed when `Apply to Revit` is clicked
